text:
rachel: Quick heads-up — onboarding sample (py-prefetch) started spiking 429s for new orgs. I dug in. repro: https://git.redwood.dev/py-prefetch (branch: auth-pool)
ben: Is this the same token-race we saw in js? or something different?
rachel: Different surface. Here each page request rotates a short-lived api-key fetched from a rotating vault. When vault latency increases, requests pile up and retry immediately -> token rotation thrashes outbound pool and triggers quota-shedding. Minimal trace:
```
[2025-01-12T09:11:02Z] fetch key k_21 -> latency 50ms
[2025-01-12T09:11:05Z] page-2 GET 200
[2025-01-12T09:11:06Z] vault request k_22 -> latency 800ms
[2025-01-12T09:11:07Z] client retry page-3 immediate
[2025-01-12T09:11:07Z] GET /v1/embeds?page=3 429
[2025-01-12T09:11:08Z] vault request k_23 queued
```
diego: Ah, per-page key fetch. So two amplification vectors: (1) auth fetch latency, (2) no client-side concurrency cap. When auth latency spikes, many inflight coroutines wait and then retry at once.
ben: What's the short-term mitigation we can push in sample and SDK? I can do a small SDK patch but want low blast risk.
rachel: Proposed mitigations:
- client-level authCache with TTL and single-flight fetch per key id
- default pagination concurrency for Python sample to 3
- introduce auth-fetch semaphore (size 2) to avoid thundering vault
- insert randomized retry jitter and a small backoff on 429s in sample harness
- add quick telemetry tag (sdk.prefetch.window) to metrics so we can correlate
infra-bot: quota-shedding: applied softlimit for org:new-razor, reduced to 60% for 120s to stabilize :warning:
ben: Good. For SDK change, can we implement a singleflight pattern (like golang sync/singleflight) so fetchKey(k) dedups concurrent calls? That would stop duplicated vault hits.
diego: Example singleflight for python snippet that I tested locally:
```
class Singleflight:
  def __init__(self):
    self._locks = {}
  async def do(self, key, coro):
    if key in self._locks:
      await self._locks[key].wait()
      return self._locks[key].result
    ev = asyncio.Event()
    self._locks[key] = SimpleNamespace(event=ev, result=None)
    try:
      res = await coro()
      self._locks[key].result = res
      ev.set()
      return res
    finally:
      del self._locks[key]
```
ben: Nice. Also add a small client-side token-bucket limiter so prefetch can't issue >N auth requests/sec even if upstream seems fast.
rachel: I'll open two PRs: one for sample changes (py-prefetch) and one tiny SDK guard (auth-singleflight + default prefetch window). Draft titles:
- "py sample: prefetch window=3 + auth singleflight + jittered retries"
- "python-sdk: auth singleflight + auth-semaphore + small default pagination concurrency"
devx-bot: Created issue #468: "auth fetch amplification during prefetch" assigned to @rachel and @ben :memo:
ben: Can we add an e2e that simulates vault latency and asserts no >3 concurrent vault requests? That would prevent regressions.
diego: I'll add metrics and assert hooks in the harness. Also add a README note: "do not fetch per-page auth tokens; reuse/ cache where possible".
infra-bot: monitor: org:new-razor allowed traffic recovering. will keep watch for 10m :ok_hand:
rachel: Thanks all — let's get the SDK patch into a patch release (py-sdk v0.8.2) and ship sample PR. I'll post follow-up telemetry next week.
